paper.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills
paper.central_claim: A single natural-language skill document can be trained as the external state of a frozen agent with deep-learning-style controls (rollout/reflection batches, bounded add/delete/replace edit budget, strict held-out validation gate, rejected-edit buffer, epoch-wise slow/meta update), giving best-or-tied accuracy on all 52 (model, benchmark, harness) cells vs no-skill, human, one-shot, Trace2Skill, TextGrad, GEPA and EvoSkill skills, with skills that transfer across model scale, harness and nearby benchmarks and add zero inference-time calls.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker by claude-kimi; model type configured by controller (agent_model=haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

sections_read: 4 Experiments (setting, baselines, main results, ablations Tables 2-3, transfer Table 4, optimizer strength Table 5, cost Table 6, learned skills)

evidence.quote: a separate optimizer model turns scored rollouts into bounded add/delete/replace edits on a single skill document, and an edit is accepted only when it strictly improves a held-out validation score
evidence.support_explanation: Core operation: optimizer-proposed bounded edits on one skill document, accepted by strict selection-split improvement.

evidence.quote: Agent skills today are hand-crafted, generated one-shot, or evolved through loosely controlled self-revision—none of which behaves like a deep-learning optimizer for the skill, and none of which reliably improves over its starting point under feedback.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: the non-weight object (skill doc) is hand-written/one-shot/loosely self-revised; the closing 'none reliably improves' premise is supported mainly by their own baseline runs (several baselines regress vs no skill in Table 1).

evidence.locator: Sec 2 Related Work, skill construction paragraph
evidence.quote: studies a narrower problem: how to train one compact domain skill with deep-learning-style controls such as trajectory batches, reflection minibatches, textual learning rates, validation gates, rejected-edit buffers, and slow/meta updates
evidence.support_explanation: Authors position the contribution against skill-construction/evolution neighbors as control machinery for one skill, not discovery or library growth.

evidence.quote: The training split supplies experience, the selection split gates updates, and the test split is used only for final reporting.
evidence.support_explanation: Three-way disjoint split: proposal data (train rollouts), commit data (selection), reporting data (test).

evidence.locator: Sec 3 Validation Gate and Rejected-Edit Buffer
evidence.quote: This gate turns reflection into propose-and-test optimization rather than unconditional self-editing
evidence.support_explanation: Gate semantic: candidate accepted if its selection score beats the current skill, best_skill exported if it beats the best so far.

evidence.locator: Sec 3 Validation Gate and Rejected-Edit Buffer
evidence.quote: Later reflection calls in the same epoch receive this buffer, so the optimizer model can avoid repeating failed edits and focus on unresolved failures.
evidence.support_explanation: Rejected edits and score drops are kept in an epoch-local buffer (reset each epoch per Algorithm 1) and read by later optimizer calls.

evidence.quote: Unbounded rewrites can erase useful rules, introduce incompatible instructions, or overfit to a local failure; bounded updates preserve continuity while still allowing the skill to acquire new procedures.
evidence.support_explanation: Rationale for the textual learning-rate (edit budget L_t).

evidence.quote: The optimizer model writes a concise longitudinal guidance block into a protected slow-update field, and this candidate is still passed through the validation gate.
evidence.support_explanation: Slow update compares same 20 training tasks under previous and current epoch skills and is gated.

evidence.quote: This meta guidance is prepended to future optimizer prompts for reflection, merging, and ranking, but it is not shipped with the target model.
evidence.support_explanation: Optimizer-side meta skill is a retained improver-side artifact; Algorithm 1 shows it is updated by the optimizer without passing through the gate.

evidence.quote: to accept or reject candidate skill edits, and all reported scores are computed on the disjoint held-out test split.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection split only gates edits; reported scores come from a disjoint test split with deterministic seed-42 splits.

evidence.quote: All baselines use the same target model, the same held-out test split, and the same scorer for every benchmark
evidence.support_explanation: Equalizes target/test/scorer, but does not say the baselines get the same optimizer model, rollout budget, or tokens as SkillOpt.

evidence.quote: Counting every (target model, benchmark, harness) cell as one comparison and the strongest of the no-skill, human-skill, LLM-skill, Trace2Skill, TextGrad, GEPA, and EvoSkill baselines as the per-cell competition,
evidence.support_explanation: Defines the 52/52 claim; per-cell competitor sets differ (see E013).

evidence.quote: EvoSkill is included for the harness-backed comparison where a matched completed run is available.
evidence.support_explanation: Codex and Claude Code cells (10 of 52) compare only against no-skill, human, LLM and EvoSkill; TextGrad/GEPA/Trace2Skill appear only in direct chat; some entries are '-'. The 'beats every competitor' claim covers different baseline sets per cell.

evidence.quote: Component ablations remove or alter one mechanism at a time, including the edit budget, rejected-edit buffer, and epoch-wise slow/meta update.
evidence.support_explanation: No ablation removes the validation gate itself, although the introduction says ablations show 'held-out gating prevents harmful proposals from accumulating'.

evidence.quote: removing the rejected-edit buffer lowers scores by 1.6, 4.6, and 2.4 points on SearchQA, SpreadsheetBench, and LiveMath, respectively
evidence.support_explanation: Buffer ablation effect sizes of 1.6-4.6 points from single runs, comparable to the unexplained spread between runs of the nominally identical default configuration (E016).

evidence.locator: Sec 4.2 Ablations, learning-rate and schedule paragraph
evidence.quote: Panel (e) confirms this on the schedule axis: constant decay scores
evidence.support_explanation: Table 2 reports the default configuration (lr=4, cosine) as 87.1/77.5/61.3 in panel (e), as 86.5/78.2/56.5 in panel (d, lr=4) and the main table gives 87.3/80.7/66.9; identical settings differ by up to ~5 points on LiveMath, an implicit measure of run-to-run noise that the paper never discusses or quantifies.

evidence.quote: removing both meta skill and slow update drops SpreadsheetBench from
evidence.support_explanation: Largest ablation effect (77.5 -> 55.0) while removing the meta skill alone costs ~2 points and SearchQA/LiveMath are non-monotone (86.3 and 59.7 without both vs 85.1 and 58.1 without meta only): the slow/meta attribution is unstable.

evidence.quote: This is direct evidence that the validation gate is doing real work: the optimizer model proposes many more edits per epoch, but only a handful pass the held-out check and survive into the deployed skill.
evidence.support_explanation: Gate attribution is argued from accepted-edit counts (1-4), not from a gate-off or random-accept control.

evidence.locator: Sec 4.3 Analysis and Transfer, cross-benchmark paragraph
evidence.quote: Cross-benchmark transfer is the strictest of the three shifts: source and target benchmarks share only the broad task family (math).
evidence.support_explanation: The only cross-benchmark transfer is OlympiadBench -> Omni-MATH (three GPT-5.4 variants, +1.3 to +3.7); cross-model transfer is within the GPT family and Codex<->Claude Code on GPT-5.5.

evidence.quote: Every remaining row in (a)–(c) is a positive transfer
evidence.support_explanation: All reported transfers are positive; no transfer with unfavorable outcome or negative control (random/unrelated skill) is shown.

evidence.quote: The practical implication is that a high-capacity frontier optimizer is the right default whenever it is available
evidence.support_explanation: Main results use a frontier optimizer (GPT-5.5) even for small targets; Table 5 (four cells) shows a target-matched optimizer recovers 56-74% of the gain, so part of the gain depends on the stronger teacher.

evidence.quote: The important deployment distinction is that this cost is paid once during skill training; after export, the optimized
evidence.support_explanation: Training-token cost is tabulated for SkillOpt only (0.6M-46.4M tokens per test point, Table 6); baseline training cost is not reported.

evidence.quote: so it is most directly applicable when the target task has automatic verifiers, exact-match metrics, executable checks, or otherwise reliable feedback signals
evidence.support_explanation: Authors state the scope boundary (verifier-backed tasks, single skill, training-distribution heuristics).

evidence.locator: Sec 3 Validation gate / Sec 4.2 Gate strictness
evidence.quote: The epoch-wise slow/meta update writes into a markup-fenced protected region of the skill document that step-level edits cannot overwrite
evidence.support_explanation: Protected region, per-edit report (edit_apply_report.json) and hash-cached selection scores make every change auditable and rollback to best skill possible.

evidence.quote: confirming that the gate tends to select skills that generalize rather than skills that only fit the selection split.
evidence.support_explanation: Figure 3 compares selection-best and test curves across epochs on three benchmarks; qualitative, single run.

evidence.quote: Together this means the headline gains are not the product of a fragile prompt-search batch size, but a genuine effect of having enough scored evidence per update.
evidence.support_explanation: Hyperparameter sweeps (Table 2) are reported on test splits and conclusions of 'insensitivity' rest on single runs; reuse of test for hyperparameter analysis is not accompanied by a statement that defaults were fixed beforehand.

evidence.quote: It first separates failures from successes and partitions each group into reflection minibatches.
evidence.support_explanation: Proposer sees full trajectories (messages, tool calls, outputs, verifier feedback); failures and successes are analysed separately then merged hierarchically with priority to failure corrections.

signatures.output: candidate skill -> selection-split score -> accepted as current / best, or rejected

signatures.feedback: native benchmark scorers on train rollouts and selection split

gap.author_gap: Skills are hand-written, one-shot, or evolved by loosely controlled self-revision; no method trains the skill with optimizer-style controls and reliably improves over its start.
gap.checked_gap: Specific and plausible: the changing non-weight object (a persistent skill artifact) and the failure of uncontrolled revision are visible in the authors' own baseline table (e.g., LLM-skill GPT-5.4 OfficeQA -29.6, TextGrad Qwen3.6-35B DocVQA/ALFWorld regressions, EvoSkill Codex SearchQA -20.4). These baselines are re-implemented by the authors, so the size of the gap is not independently confirmed.
gap.lineage: Reflective prompt optimization (TextGrad, GEPA) -> trajectory-to-skill distillation (Trace2Skill) -> skill-folder evolution under failure analysis (EvoSkill); SkillOpt adds batch/edit-budget/gate/buffer/slow-update controls on a single skill.
gap.closest_adjacent: EvoSkill (harness-side skill evolution), Trace2Skill (no gate), GEPA/TextGrad (prompt, not persistent skill). Other gated document-rewriting and playbook-curation optimizers (e.g., ACE-style playbooks) are not compared; the 'first systematic controllable optimizer' claim rests on the cited set.
gap.residue: Control set (budget, gate, buffer, slow/meta) is a bundle; which part matters is only partly separated; baseline optimizer parity unspecified.
gap.stakes: Domain adaptation of frozen (often closed) frontier agents without weight access; large baseline-to-trained gaps on procedural tasks.
gap.method_response: Treat the skill as trainable state with bounded, validated, auditable edits, keeping the deployed skill small and inference cost zero.
gap.remaining_gap: Single skill per domain, verifier-backed tasks only, teacher-strength dependence, gate noise handling, no statistical treatment.
unresolved: Whether baseline optimizers received comparable rollouts/teacher/tokens.
Contribution of gating vs bounded edits vs teacher strength is not separated by a gate-off control.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Deployed adaptation is a conditioning text (the skill) given to a frozen model with no per-task parameter update, and the paper checks generality over six benchmarks, seven models, three harnesses. Sub-card C03 requires teaching a model to parse a canonical schema in an upstream tuning phase or retrieving a reference substrate; SkillOpt does neither (the upstream phase is an offline text optimizer), so sub_id is null. Step 4/5 of C03 (category-level holdout, contamination audit, cheaper alternative under equal budget) are only partly done: model/harness/one-benchmark transfers exist, no contamination audit, human and one-shot skills serve as cheaper alternatives but optimizer budgets are not equalised.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: 'win in a characterised regime' partial (largest gains on procedural tasks, small on near-ceiling SearchQA); 'ablation toggling conditioning signal' met via no-skill vs skill. Failure: 'obvious cheaper alternative omitted' not triggered (human/LLM skills); 'ablations too shallow' partly applicable (no gate-off).
matches.reason: The operation actually executed is optimization of a conditioning artifact for a frozen model; the original card's own mechanism (learning to read a schema) is absent, so the match is weak and recorded as partial.

rs_pattern.reason: Closest original card is adapt_via_conditioning; no sub-card applies. Reframe-as-solvable-object was considered (training analogy) but no correspondence or solver import is made, so it is not assigned.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: held-out gains over uncontrolled alternatives are reported, but gate/budget attribution and baseline parity are unresolved.

matches.condition_checks: H10 steps: collect successes and failures (met), aggregate before editing via minibatch + hierarchical merge (met), localize edits to atomic ops and gate on a disjoint split (met), spend evaluation deliberately (partial: ranking/clip, hash cache, but not bandit/tree), report without test selection (met on main table; hyperparameter panels use test). F-checks: loop not just transplanted to a domain (met, six benchmarks); self-built validation (avoided).
Proposal/commit separation and fallback to current skill met; strict-greater rule and exported best skill; but no statistic matched to noise, no per-edit counterfactual credit, no gate-off ablation.

unassigned: Optimizer-side meta skill (ungated improver memory) has no clean H19/H21 fit because the optimizer itself is not edited with a validated procedure.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS 'express adaptation as conditioning without parameter updates' = the conditioning artifact is the single skill document rewritten by directed critique edits (H10).
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: RS card concerns teaching a model to read a format; here the model is untouched and the conditioning text itself is optimized by a teacher.

expectations.reason: Successes fed with failures, bounded edit budget, strictly-greater gate, hash-cached best skill; protected slow-update region.
Minibatch reflection and hierarchical merge with support counts aggregate across trajectories before editing.

expectations.reason: Edits are localized text operations, but failures are not attributed to sections or defects-vs-lapses; attribution accuracy is not measured.

expectations.applies_when: Self-constructed validation replaces ground truth (status met = failure avoided)
expectations.reason: Native benchmark scorers with real verifiers (spreadsheet runtime, exact match) are used on selection and test.

expectations.applies_when: The gate is a claimed contributor
expectations.reason: The gate is a separable component but no gate-off / random-accept ablation is run; the claim rests on accepted-edit counts.
Whole-candidate counterfactual versus current skill on the selection split, but individual edits are not credited separately.
Training tokens and cost per point are tabulated for SkillOpt only; optimizer API cost and baseline cost are not reported.
Proposal data are training rollouts; commit data are a disjoint selection split; test is separate.
Plain strict-greater rule on the selection score; no paired test, margin or repeated evaluation; selection-split sizes are not stated in the main text.
Human and one-shot LLM skills are included as cheaper conditioning alternatives; equal-budget optimizer baselines are not shown.
No contamination analysis for public benchmarks (SearchQA, DocVQA, ALFWorld) is reported in the material searched.

Optimizer model, rollout count and token budget of TextGrad/GEPA/Trace2Skill/EvoSkill relative to SkillOpt are not stated.

claims.text: SkillOpt is best or tied on all 52 (model, benchmark, harness) cells and averages +23.5 (GPT-5.5 direct chat) over no skill.
claims.setting: 6 benchmarks x 7 target models (direct chat) plus GPT-5.5 under Codex and Claude Code; native scorers; test split disjoint from selection
claims.baseline_control: no skill, human, one-shot LLM, Trace2Skill, TextGrad, GEPA (direct chat only), EvoSkill (harness only)
claims.selection_vs_test: selection split gates edits; test only for final report
claims.result_denominator: 52 cells; some margins are tiny or ties (e.g., GPT-5.4-mini LiveMath 32.8 vs Trace2Skill 32.8); single run, no CI
claims.counterevidence: Baseline sets differ by cell; no seeds; baseline optimizer budgets unspecified.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Under the authors' single-run protocol the evolved skill has the highest held-out point estimate in all listed cells; margins vs the strongest baseline are often within the ~2-5 point spread seen between identical-config runs.

claims.text: Bounded textual learning, held-out gating, rejected-edit buffer and slow/meta update explain the gains.
claims.setting: GPT-5.5 as target and optimizer on SearchQA, SpreadsheetBench, LiveMath
claims.baseline_control: ablated variants (no lr, no buffer, no meta/slow)
claims.counterevidence: No gate-off ablation; non-monotone slow/meta rows; run noise comparable to small effects.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Removing the slow/meta update on SpreadsheetBench and removing the edit budget lower results; the gate's own contribution is inferred, not measured.

claims.text: Optimized skills transfer across model scales, execution harnesses and a nearby benchmark without further optimization.
claims.setting: GPT-5.4 -> mini/nano (Spreadsheet, LiveMath); Codex <-> Claude Code on GPT-5.5; OlympiadBench -> Omni-MATH on three GPT-5.4 variants
claims.selection_vs_test: transferred skills evaluated on target test splits
claims.counterevidence: No negative-control skill (random/unrelated) or non-GPT-family model transfer; math-only cross-benchmark.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Positive transfer within the tested neighborhoods (GPT-family, two harnesses, math).

claims.text: The deployed skill is compact (<2000 tokens), arises from 1-4 accepted edits and adds no inference cost.
claims.counterevidence: Training cost is large for some benchmarks (213.8M tokens on SearchQA) and baseline costs are not reported.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Inference-time overhead is only skill length; training cost is paid up front and is not compared with baselines.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A skill document edited by a frontier optimizer under a strict selection-split gate improves held-out test scores of frozen agents versus no skill and versus the compared hand-written, one-shot and re-implemented optimizer baselines in most reported cells, and the exported skill transfers positively to nearby models, harnesses and a nearby math benchmark (author-reported single runs).
assessment.cannot_claim: That the validation gate or any single control causally explains the gains; that baselines had matched optimizer budgets; statistical significance of 52/52; improver-level gain from the meta skill; broad cross-domain transfer; our own reproduction.

G.reason: Concrete non-weight object (persistent skill document) and a specific limitation of uncontrolled revision, supported by observed regressions of one-shot and loosely controlled baselines; nearest neighbors (Trace2Skill, EvoSkill, GEPA, TextGrad) are named and compared; 'first systematic controllable optimizer' and ACE-style playbook neighbors are not checked; remaining gaps (single skill, verifier dependence) are stated.

M.reason: Rollout evidence -> minibatch reflection -> hierarchical merge -> ranked, clipped edit -> gate is a coherent mechanism with an explicit rationale for each control (continuity, noise, drift); distinguishes itself from unbounded rewrite with testable predictions, but credit attribution among controls is only partly tested and the training analogy carries little predictive content.

X.reason: Operation chain, information visibility, acceptance rule (strict >, ties rejected), hash-cached scores, best-skill export, per-edit reports, protected slow-update region, epoch-local buffer and full optimizer prompt contracts are specified and reconstructable; scope limits (verifiers, single skill) are stated. Residual weaknesses (no noise handling, buffer reset each epoch) are recorded under E.statistics and E.causality rather than double-counted.

E.measurement.reason: Native hard-success/exact-match scorers on six diverse benchmarks, real execution runtimes (openpyxl/pandas, Codex, Claude Code) and a deterministic seed-42 split; no self-built validators. Test-set sizes are mostly unstated and no trivial-baseline sanity check (e.g., answer-format-only skill) is reported.

E.causality.reason: Informative ablations (edit budget, buffer, slow/meta, optimizer strength, training size) and no-skill/human/one-shot baselines exist, but no gate-off control despite the gate claim, baseline optimizer/budget parity is unspecified, effect sizes sit near unexplained run-to-run spread, and a strong teacher is used for small targets (partly addressed by four-cell Table 5).

E.holdout.reason: Clean three-way split with selection used only for gating and a disjoint test for all headline numbers; transfer tests across model/harness/benchmark add independent-task evidence. Hyperparameter panels are reported on test and no contamination analysis is given for public benchmarks; cross-benchmark transfer is math-only.

E.statistics.reason: Single-run point estimates for 52 cells and all ablations, no seeds, intervals or tests; some split sizes stated (ALFWorld 140/134) but most are not; identical configurations differ by several points across tables. Sensitivity sweeps give only indirect spread information.

E.cost.reason: Training tokens, initial/final skill length, accepted edits and cost per point are tabulated and deployment overhead is clear, but optimizer-side API cost, wall-clock, and baseline training budgets are missing, so budget fairness is unknown.

rationale: 单一技能文档的受限文本编辑+严格选择集门控,训练/选择/测试三分,跨模型/框架迁移均为正。无gate-off对照,基线预算未对齐,单次运行无方差,相同配置跨表差达数分。判定retained/scoped。
